about: Condescending Wonka shows Gene Wilder as Willy Wonka in the 1971 film Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory, resting his chin on his hand with a thin smile, tilted head and half-lidded eyes. That look of fake interest is what the meme runs on: the captions are mock-polite replies to someone bragging, overexplaining or stating the obvious. Wonka never openly mocks them; he just asks a leading question or says "tell me more" in a way that makes it clear he is not impressed at all. It is the reaction image for humblebrags and people who think one small achievement makes them an expert.
origin: The still is from the 1971 Paramount musical starring Gene Wilder. It spread as an advice-animal style image macro in early 2011, and the sarcastic "oh, you..." caption style quickly became its standard format.
usage:
Top box: start with a sarcastic setup that repeats what the other person said, often "oh, you..." ("oh, you watched one documentary?"). Bottom box: the deadpan conclusion that exaggerates their claim ("you must be a doctor now").

The humor depends on the tone staying fake-friendly. Avoid openly insulting the target; let Wonka's smirk do the mocking. It is best aimed at self-appointed experts, crypto tips, gym beginners, people who "don't watch TV" and anyone who mentions their diet unprompted.
